summary: This React component creates a 'TL;DR' (summary) section for blog posts that displays user-provided content while also inserting JSON-LD structured data into the page head so search engines understand the summary is an abstract. It recursively extracts plain text from the React children to populate the structured data, and includes accessibility labels so screen readers know what the section is.

explanations.8: This function takes any type of React content and converts it to plain text by checking each possible type: strings pass through, numbers get converted to strings, arrays get flattened by processing each item, and React element objects get their children extracted recursively.
explanations.13: We're using optional chaining (?.) to safely access nested properties on an object that might be undefined or null without causing errors.
explanations.25: useMemo caches the structured data object so it only recalculates when the children prop changes, avoiding unnecessary recreations.
explanations.37: We're inserting a JSON-LD script tag (a format search engines recognize) into the document head via Docusaurus's Head component.
explanations.43: The translate function pulls user-facing text from a localization system, allowing the aria-label to be translated to different languages.
